# Changelog

The full history is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/s00d/onlinesim-java-api/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## 2.1.1

- Fixed models against the current API: `Profile.number()`/`country()`, `Operation.response()` may be `null`, `RentSms.code()` `"0"` for `notify` SMS; `paymentHistory().paylist()` is kept when it arrives as a list.
- `waitCode` retries `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` (rate limit), `ERROR_UNDEFINED` and `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`.
- `MockOnlineSim` follows the backend more closely: rent reservation and confirmation, `setOperationRevise` and `closeRentNum` answers, missing vs wrong key — see [Testing](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-java-api/testing).

## 2.1.0

- New: `MockOnlineSim` (`ru.onlinesim.mock`), an offline fake of the API for your tests — see [Testing](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-java-api/testing).
- Release automation: tags `vX.Y.Z` publish to Maven Central from CI.

## 2.0.0

A rewrite with a new API; v1 code does not compile unchanged.

- Same coordinates as 1.x, new major version: `ru.onlinesim:onlinesim-api:2.0.0`. Java 11+.
- One client, `new OnlineSim(apiKey)` or `OnlineSim.builder()`, with the sections as accessors: `client.numbers()`, `client.rent()`, `client.user()`, `client.free()`.
- HTTP through `java.net.http.HttpClient` behind a `Transport` interface; the only dependency is Gson. No Apache HttpClient, dotenv or Consul.
- The key is sent as a Bearer header, never in the URL; the base URL is configurable and HTTPS by default.
- Unchecked exceptions: `ApiException`, `NoNumberException`, `TransportException`, `WaitTimeoutException`.
- `numbers().waitCode` with `Duration` interval and timeout, `keepOpen`, `since`; retries network errors.
- `rent().get` creates extendable rents by default (`extension = true`).
- New: `user().setWebhookUrl` / `clearWebhookUrl` / `webhookLogs`, `OnlineSim.parseWebhook`.
- Removed: the proxy API, `numbers.repeat`, `numbers.service`, `numbers.serviceNumber`, `rent.portReload`, `user.createEmpty`, the old free-number endpoints (use `free().list`).


# Free numbers

## list

Countries, the numbers of the selected country and the SMS of the selected number, in one call.

```java
FreeList list()
FreeList list(FreeListOptions options)
```

| Option    | Type     | Default        | Description                                                      |
| --------- | -------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `country` | `int`    | `44` (server)  | Country code; an unknown one falls back to the first available.  |
| `number`  | `String` | first number   | Number **without** the country code, as the keys of `numbers()`. |
| `page`    | `int`    | `1`            | Page of `messages()`.                                            |
| `count`   | `int`    | server default | SMS per page, 10–500.                                            |

Unset options are not sent. `FreeList`:

- `countries()`: `List<FreeList.Country>` — `country()`, `countryText()`, `countryOriginal()`
- `numbers()`: `Map<String, FreeList.Phone>` keyed by the short number — `country()`, `countryOriginal()`, `fullNumber()`, `dataHumans()`, `isArchive()`
- `messages()`: `FreeList.Messages`, a `Paginator<FreeList.Message>` plus `number()` and `country()`; a message has `id()`, `text()`, `inNumber()`, `myNumber()`, `code()` (`-` when no code was found), `createdAt()`, `dataHumans()`

```java
FreeList uk = client.free().list(FreeListOptions.defaults().country(44));
Optional<String> first = uk.numbers().keySet().stream().findFirst();
if (first.isPresent()) {
  FreeList page = client.free().list(FreeListOptions.defaults().country(44).number(first.get()).count(20));
  for (FreeList.Message sms : page.messages().data()) {
    System.out.println(sms.inNumber() + " " + sms.code() + " " + sms.text());
  }
}
```


# Numbers

An operation (`tzid`) is one ordered number. Order it with `get`/`getWithNumber`, read the SMS with `stateOne` or `waitCode`, finish it with `close` (or `ban`). Countries are phone codes (`7`, `44`, …), services are slugs (`google`, `vkcom`, …) as returned by `tariffs`. Every `country` parameter defaults to `7` in the shorter overloads.

## price

Price of one number, USD; `null` when the country has no price for the service.

```java
Double price(String service)
Double price(String service, int country)
```

| Param     | Type     | Default | Description   |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------- |
| `service` | `String` | —       | Service slug. |
| `country` | `int`    | `7`     | Country code. |

```java
Double usd = client.numbers().price("google", 44);
```

Errors: `ApiException` `ERROR_NO_SERVICE`, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY`.

## get

Order a number; returns the operation id. Freezes the price on the balance.

```java
long get(String service)
long get(String service, int country)
long get(String service, int country, Collection<String> reject)
```

| Param     | Type                 | Default      | Description                                      |
| --------- | -------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `service` | `String`             | —            | Service slug.                                    |
| `country` | `int`                | `7`          | Country code.                                    |
| `reject`  | `Collection<String>` | profile list | Number prefixes to skip, e.g. `List.of("4470")`. |

```java
long tzid = client.numbers().get("google", 44, List.of("4470"));
```

Errors: `NoNumberException`; `ApiException` `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE`, `ERROR_NO_SERVICE`, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY`, `EXCEEDED_CONCURRENT_OPERATIONS`, `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER`.

## getWithNumber

Same as `get`, but returns the number right away.

```java
NumberOrder getWithNumber(String service)
NumberOrder getWithNumber(String service, int country)
NumberOrder getWithNumber(String service, int country, Collection<String> reject)
```

`NumberOrder`: `tzid()`, `number()` (with `+`), `country()`, `time()` (seconds left), `service()`, `title()`, `guardIntervalRemainingSeconds()` (seconds until the operation may be closed).

```java
NumberOrder order = client.numbers().getWithNumber("google", 44);
System.out.println(order.tzid() + " " + order.number());
```

Errors: as `get`.

## state

All operations of the account; an empty list when there are none.

```java
List<Operation> state()
List<Operation> state(StateOptions options)
```

| Option          | Type                 | Default | Description                                                       |
| --------------- | -------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `messageToCode` | `boolean`            | `true`  | `msg()` is the code only; `false` — the full SMS text.            |
| `orderBy`       | `StateOptions.Order` | `ASC`   | Order of operations.                                              |
| `msgList`       | `boolean`            | `false` | All SMS in `msgList()` (`List<OperationSms>`) instead of `msg()`. |

`Operation`: `tzid()`, `response()`, `number()`, `service()`, `country()`, `sum()`, `time()`, `msg()`, `msgList()`, `guardIntervalRemainingSeconds()`, ….
`response()` is the state: `TZ_INPOOL` (number being assigned), `TZ_NUM_WAIT` (waiting for SMS), `TZ_NUM_ANSWER` (SMS arrived), `TZ_OVER_OK` (finished), `ERROR_NO_ITEMS` (failed), or `null` when the server sent no state (no number could be issued). `msg()` is `null` until the first SMS. The server caches answers for a few seconds.

```java
StateOptions newestFirst = StateOptions.defaults().orderBy(StateOptions.Order.DESC);
for (Operation op : client.numbers().state(newestFirst)) {
  System.out.println(op.tzid() + " " + op.response() + " " + op.msg());
}
```

## stateOne

One operation. Takes the same `StateOptions`; `orderBy` is ignored.

```java
Operation stateOne(long tzid)
Operation stateOne(long tzid, StateOptions options)
```

```java
Operation op = client.numbers().stateOne(tzid);
if ("TZ_NUM_ANSWER".equals(op.response())) System.out.println(op.msg()); // response() may be null
```

Errors: `ApiException` `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` when the operation does not exist (any more).

## waitCode

Poll the operation until a code arrives, then close it and return the code. Blocks the calling thread.

```java
String waitCode(long tzid)
String waitCode(long tzid, WaitOptions options)
```

| Option             | Type                           | Default | Description                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interval`         | `Duration`                     | 5 s     | Poll interval.                                                       |
| `timeout`          | `Duration`                     | 10 min  | Give up after.                                                       |
| `keepOpen`         | `boolean`                      | `false` | Call `next(tzid)` instead of `close(tzid)`, to wait for another SMS. |
| `fullMessage`      | `boolean`                      | `false` | Return the full SMS text instead of the code.                        |
| `since`            | `String`                       | `null`  | Ignore this value (the previous code).                               |
| `sleeper`, `clock` | `WaitOptions.Sleeper`, `Clock` | real    | Injectable for tests.                                                |

Transient errors are retried until the timeout: `TransportException`, and `ApiException` `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` (the HTTP 429 rate limit), `ERROR_UNDEFINED` and `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`. Any other `ApiException` is thrown at once. An interrupt stops the wait with `OnlineSimException` and keeps the thread's interrupt flag.

```java
String first = client.numbers().waitCode(tzid, WaitOptions.defaults().keepOpen(true));
String second = client.numbers().waitCode(tzid, WaitOptions.defaults().since(first).timeout(Duration.ofMinutes(5)));
```

Errors: `WaitTimeoutException`; `ApiException` with code `TZ_OVER_OK` or `ERROR_NO_ITEMS` when the operation ended without a new code; any other `ApiException` from `stateOne`/`close`/`next`.

## next

Switch the operation to its next SMS and keep it open (for services that send several SMS).

```java
void next(long tzid)
```

```java
client.numbers().next(tzid);
```

Errors: `ApiException` `ERROR_WRONG_TZID` (not an operation of your account), `ERROR_NO_TZID`.

## close

Finish the operation. An operation without SMS can be closed only after its guard interval (`guardIntervalRemainingSeconds()`); every attempt locks the tzid for 5 s.

```java
void close(long tzid)
```

```java
client.numbers().close(tzid);
```

Errors: `ApiException` `NO_COMPLETE_TZID`, `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`, `ERROR_WRONG_TZID`.

## ban

Finish the operation and report the number as bad. Only before any SMS arrived.

```java
void ban(long tzid)
```

```java
client.numbers().ban(tzid);
```

Errors: as `close`; `ApiException` with code `"0"` when the operation already has an SMS — nothing is changed then.

## tariffs

Services, prices and stock of every country, keyed by country code. No API key needed. The answer is large (a few MB); prefer `tariffsOne`.

```java
Map<String, CountryStat> tariffs()
```

`CountryStat`: `name()`, `localeName()`, `position()`, `code()`, `other()`, `isNew()`, `enabled()`, `services()`; `services()` maps `service_<slug>` to `ServiceStat`: `count()` (`null` when unknown), `popular()`, `code()`, `price()`, `id()`, `service()`, `slug()`.

```java
Map<String, CountryStat> all = client.numbers().tariffs();
System.out.println(all.size() + " countries");
```

## tariffsOne

Services, prices and stock of one country.

```java
CountryStat tariffsOne()
CountryStat tariffsOne(int country)
```

```java
CountryStat uk = client.numbers().tariffsOne(44);
for (ServiceStat s : uk.services().values()) System.out.println(s.slug() + " " + s.price() + " " + s.count());
```

Errors: `ApiException` `NO_COUNTRY`.


# Rent

A rent keeps a number for `days` days. Its SMS come in `RentItem.messages()`, newest first.

`get` reserves the price (it shows in `zbalance`): the rent starts with `status()` `0` and `checked()` `false` and waits up to 20 minutes for its first SMS. The first SMS that is not a `notify` notice confirms it (`status()` `1`) and charges the price; without one the rent closes and the reservation is released. Some countries (`confirm` in `tariffs`, e.g. US numbers) are confirmed and charged at once.

`RentItem`: `tzid()`, `status()`, `number()`, `country()`, `sum()`, `days()`, `hours()`, `time()`, `timeSeconds()`, `extension()`, `extend()`, `messages()`, `startTime()`, `stopTime()`, `dayExtend()`, … —
`sum()` is the cost in USD incl. extensions (a `double`; the server sends a number, or a decimal string in `state`), `time()` minutes left, `timeSeconds()` seconds left,
`extension()` `0` not extendable / `1` extendable / `2` auto-extension, `extend()` maps days to the extension price (empty when not extendable),
`messages()` is `List<RentSms>`: `id()`, `service()`, `text()`, `code()`, `createdAt()` — `code()` is `""` when no code was found and `"0"` for a `notify` SMS (a prohibited sender; the server sends the integer `0`).

## get

Rent a number. The price is reserved; the first SMS charges it.

```java
RentItem get()
RentItem get(int country)
RentItem get(int country, int days)
RentItem get(int country, int days, boolean extension)
```

| Param       | Type      | Default | Description                                     |
| ----------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `country`   | `int`     | `7`     | Country code.                                   |
| `days`      | `int`     | `1`     | One of the tariff's `days()` keys.              |
| `extension` | `boolean` | `true`  | `false` makes the rent non-extendable for good. |

```java
RentItem rent = client.rent().get(7, 7);
System.out.println(rent.tzid() + " " + rent.number() + " " + rent.sum());
```

Errors: `NoNumberException`; `ApiException` `UNDEFINED_DAYS`, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY`, `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE`, `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER`.

## state

All rents of the account.

```java
List<RentItem> state()
```

```java
for (RentItem rent : client.rent().state()) {
  System.out.println(rent.number() + " " + (rent.messages().isEmpty() ? "-" : rent.messages().get(0).code()));
}
```

## stateOne

One rent.

```java
RentItem stateOne(long tzid)
```

```java
List<RentSms> messages = client.rent().stateOne(tzid).messages();
```

Errors: `ApiException` `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` for an unknown tzid.

## extend

Extend a rent by `days` days and charge the balance at once. Only confirmed rents (`status()` `1`) created with `extension = true`.

```java
RentItem extend(long tzid)
RentItem extend(long tzid, int days)
```

```java
RentItem rent = client.rent().extend(tzid, 3);
System.out.println(rent.stopTime());
```

Errors: `ApiException` `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` (unknown tzid, not confirmed yet or closed, not extendable, unknown period, a repeat within 10 s), `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE`.

## close

Return the number before the period ends. A rent that is not confirmed yet (`status()` `0`) and has no SMS can be closed only after 120 s; then, or with only `notify` SMS, the reservation is released. With a real SMS the rent is confirmed (charged) and closed. A confirmed rent closes without a refund. US numbers cannot be closed early.

```java
void close(long tzid)
```

```java
client.rent().close(tzid);
```

Errors: `ApiException` `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` (unknown tzid), `NO_COMPLETE_TZID`, `NO_CLOSE_RENT_US`, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER`.

## tariffs

Rent prices of every country, keyed by country code. No API key needed.

```java
Map<String, RentTariff> tariffs()
```

`RentTariff`: `code()`, `name()`, `enabled()`, `isNew()`, `position()`, `extend()`, `confirm()`, `days()`, `count()`, `extCounts()` — `days()` maps rent days to the price in USD, `count()` to the numbers available.

```java
Map<String, RentTariff> tariffs = client.rent().tariffs();
```

## tariffsOne

Rent prices of one country.

```java
RentTariff tariffsOne()
RentTariff tariffsOne(int country)
```

```java
Map<String, Double> days = client.rent().tariffsOne(7).days();
System.out.println(days.get("7")); // price of 7 days
```

Errors: `ApiException` `NO_COUNTRY` for a country without rent.


# Testing

`MockOnlineSim` (package `ru.onlinesim.mock`) is an in-process fake of the OnlineSim API that ships in the main jar. It is a `Transport` that answers like the real backend — same shapes, same error codes, HTTP 456 for a wrong key and HTTP 200 `ERROR_WRONG_KEY` for a missing one — and keeps a balance, operations and rents. Your code talks to a normal `OnlineSim` client, so nothing in it changes for tests. It is deterministic: no randomness, no clock, numbers and ids come from a counter. Thread-safe: requests and test helpers are serialised.

## Setup

```java
import ru.onlinesim.OnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOptions;

MockOnlineSim mock = new MockOnlineSim(MockOptions.defaults().balance(10));
OnlineSim client = mock.client(); // an OnlineSim wired to the mock
```

```java
new MockOnlineSim()
new MockOnlineSim(MockOptions options)

MockOptions.defaults()
    .apiKey(String apiKey)                                   // default "mock-key"
    .balance(double usd)                                     // default 100
    .prices(Map<Integer, Map<String, Double>> prices)        // country → service → USD
    .rentTariffs(Map<Integer, MockRentTariff> rentTariffs)   // country → new MockRentTariff(days → USD, extend)
    .guardInterval(int seconds)                              // default 0
```

| Option          | Default                                                                         | Description                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiKey`        | `"mock-key"`                                                                    | Key the mock accepts. `mock.client()` uses it; `mock.client(b -> b.apiKey("x"))` tests a wrong key.             |
| `balance`       | `100`                                                                           | Starting balance, USD.                                                                                          |
| `prices`        | `{7: {vkcom: 0.5, telegram: 1.2, google: 0.3}, 44: {google: 0.2, vkcom: 0.36}}` | Number prices; replaces the defaults. Also feeds `numbers().tariffs()`.                                         |
| `rentTariffs`   | `{7: MockRentTariff({1: 1.0, 3: 2.5, 7: 5.0}, extend = true)}`                  | Rent prices; `extend = false` makes rents of that country non-extendable.                                       |
| `guardInterval` | `0`                                                                             | `> 0`: an operation without SMS, or an unconfirmed rent without any SMS, cannot be closed (`NO_COMPLETE_TZID`). |

`mock.client(Consumer<OnlineSim.Builder>)` takes the usual [client options](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-java-api/#client-options); the transport is always the mock's. To build the client yourself, pass `mock.transport()`; any `baseUrl` works:

```java
import ru.onlinesim.OnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOnlineSim;

MockOnlineSim mock = new MockOnlineSim();
OnlineSim client = OnlineSim.builder().apiKey("mock-key").transport(mock.transport()).build();
```

## A full example

Order a number, let an SMS arrive while `waitCode` polls, check the code and the money. `addSmsAfter` delivers the SMS after a number of polls instead of after some time, so `waitCode` runs with a no-op sleeper and the test takes milliseconds.

```java
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import ru.onlinesim.NumberOrder;
import ru.onlinesim.OnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.WaitOptions;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOptions;

class ReceiveCodeTest {
    @Test
    void receivesTheCode() {
        MockOnlineSim mock = new MockOnlineSim(MockOptions.defaults().balance(10));
        OnlineSim client = mock.client();

        NumberOrder order = client.numbers().getWithNumber("google", 44);
        assertEquals("+44900000001", order.number());

        mock.addSmsAfter(order.tzid(), "Your Google code: 123-456", 2); // the third poll sees it
        String code = client.numbers().waitCode(order.tzid(), WaitOptions.defaults().sleeper(d -> {}));

        assertEquals("123456", code);
        assertEquals("TZ_OVER_OK", mock.operations().get(0).status()); // waitCode closed it
        assertEquals(9.8, mock.balance()); // the price is spent once an SMS arrived
    }
}
```

The `msg` of an operation is the code by default: the first run of 4–8 digits, with spaces and dashes between digits removed (`123-456` → `123456`); a text without such a run comes back whole. `messageToCode(false)` (or `fullMessage(true)` in `waitCode`) gives the full text.

## Errors

`failNext(code)` makes the next request answer `{"response": code}` — the client turns it into `ApiException` (or `NoNumberException`) exactly as for the real server. Pass an endpoint to fail only that endpoint. `failNextTransport()` makes the next request fail with a non-JSON HTTP 502 (`TransportException`).

```java
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import ru.onlinesim.NoNumberException;
import ru.onlinesim.OnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.TransportException;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOnlineSim;

class FailuresTest {
    @Test
    void handlesAMissingNumberAndANetworkHiccup() {
        MockOnlineSim mock = new MockOnlineSim();
        OnlineSim client = mock.client();

        mock.failNext("NO_NUMBER", "getNum.php");
        assertThrows(NoNumberException.class, () -> client.numbers().get("google"));

        mock.failNextTransport(503);
        assertThrows(TransportException.class, () -> client.user().balance());

        assertEquals(100, client.user().balance().balance()); // one-shot
    }
}
```

The state itself produces the real error codes too: `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE` when the balance is short, `NO_NUMBER` when `reject` matches the next number, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY` / `ERROR_NO_SERVICE` for unknown prices, `ERROR_WRONG_TZID` for an unknown or closed operation (`next` too; `ERROR_NO_TZID` for tzid `0`), `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY` / `UNDEFINED_DAYS` for an unknown rent country or period, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` for every refused `rent().extend`, `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` for an unknown rent in `rent().close`, `ERROR_WRONG_KEY` for a wrong key (HTTP 456) or no key (HTTP 200).

## Inspecting requests

`mock.requests()` lists every request received as `MockRequest`: `method()`, `path()` (relative to `/api/`), `query()` (decoded, in the order sent) and `body()` (the JSON of a POST as sent, `null` for a GET).

```java
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockOnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.mock.MockRequest;

class RejectTest {
    @Test
    void sendsRejectAsACommaList() {
        MockOnlineSim mock = new MockOnlineSim();
        mock.client().numbers().get("google", 44, List.of("4470", "4471"));

        MockRequest req = mock.requests().get(0);
        assertEquals("getNum.php", req.path());
        assertEquals(Map.of("service", "google", "country", "44", "reject", "4470,4471", "lang", "en"), req.query());
    }
}
```

## Control API

| Member                                                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client()` / `client(Consumer<OnlineSim.Builder>)`                                          | A normal `OnlineSim` wired to the mock.                                                                                                     |
| `transport()`                                                                               | The fake `Transport`.                                                                                                                       |
| `addSms(tzid, text)` / `addSms(tzid, text, service)`                                        | An SMS arrives now at a number operation or a rent (detected by `tzid`). Throws `IllegalStateException` for an unknown or closed one.       |
| `addSmsAfter(tzid, text, polls)` / `addSmsAfter(tzid, text, polls, service)`                | The SMS arrives after `polls` state requests for `tzid` (`numbers().state()`/`stateOne`, `rent().state()`/`stateOne`).                      |
| `failNext(code)` / `failNext(code, endpoint)`                                               | The next request (to `endpoint` only, e.g. `"getNum.php"`) answers `{"response": code}`.                                                    |
| `failNextTransport()` / `failNextTransport(status)` / `failNextTransport(status, endpoint)` | The next request fails with a non-JSON body and HTTP `status` (default `502`).                                                              |
| `setBalance(usd)` / `balance()`                                                             | Set / read the total balance, USD (it includes the part frozen by open operations and unconfirmed rents, as `user().balance()` reports it). |
| `operations()` / `rents()`                                                                  | Snapshots of the current number operations (`MockOperation`) / open rents (`MockRent`), for assertions.                                     |
| `requests()`                                                                                | Log of the requests received (`MockRequest`).                                                                                               |
| `reset()`                                                                                   | Back to the constructor's state.                                                                                                            |

## What the mock does

- **Numbers**: `get` freezes the price; `close` after an SMS spends it, `close` without one refunds it; `ban` after an SMS answers `"0"`, like the server. Numbers are `+<country>9000000NN`, ids count from 1. `next` switches to the following SMS. The operation's `time` stays at 1200 s — there is no clock.
- **Rent**: `get` reserves the price (`status()` `0`, `checked()` `false`) and keeps the `extension` flag; the first SMS that is not `notify` confirms the rent (`status()` `1`) and charges it — `addSms(tzid, text, "notify")` adds a notice with `code` `0` that confirms nothing. `extend` works on a confirmed rent and charges at once. `close` releases the reservation of an unconfirmed rent and gives no refund for a confirmed one. `sum` is a number in `get`/`extend` and a decimal string on the wire of `state`, like the server. SMS appear in `messages()`, newest first.
- **User**: `balance` (frozen part included), a fixed profile, `setWebhookUrl` accepts any `scheme://…` URL (`VALIDATION_ERROR` otherwise), `webhookLogs` lists the deliveries the mock *recorded* when an SMS arrived while a webhook URL was set — it makes no HTTP call; their `params` follow the real payload (`code` `""` without a code, rent `number` in digits without `+`, rent `timeLeft` in minutes). `paymentHistory` has no orders.
- **Free**: `free().list()` returns two fixed countries (44 first) with one number and a few SMS each; `count` is clamped to 10..500.
- Not imitated: anything that needs real time — the 5 s lock after `setOperationOk` (`INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`), the 10 s lock of `rent().extend`, the 120 s before an unconfirmed rent may be closed and its 20-minute wait for the first SMS. `guardInterval > 0` stands in for "too early to close".


# User

## balance

Balance in USD.

```java
Balance balance()
```

`Balance`: `balance()` includes the sum frozen by numbers and unconfirmed rents in progress (`zbalance()`, which may be negative): available = `balance() − max(zbalance(), 0)`. `income()` is the partner income (`null` when not sent). The server caches the answer for 60 s.

```java
Balance b = client.user().balance();
double available = b.balance() - Math.max(b.zbalance(), 0);
```

Errors: `ApiException` `ERROR_WRONG_KEY`, `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`, `API_ACCESS_DISABLED`, `API_ACCESS_IP`.

## profile

The account profile.

```java
Profile profile()
```

`Profile`: `id()`, `name()`, `username()`, `email()`, `locale()`, `currency()`, `numberCountry()`, `numberReject()` (`List<String>`), `webhookUrl()`, `apiAccess()` (`true`, `false` when API access is disabled in the profile, or a map of allowed IPs, as a Gson `JsonElement`), `number()` (`Long`, `null` when no phone is linked), `country()` (`String` or `null`), ….

```java
Profile p = client.user().profile();
System.out.println(p.email() + " " + p.webhookUrl());
```

## paymentHistory

Top-up orders (paginated, newest first) and the available payment methods.

```java
PaymentHistory paymentHistory()
PaymentHistory paymentHistory(int page)
```

`PaymentHistory`: `orders()` (`Paginator<PaymentOrder>`), `paylist()`, `domains()`, `forms()`, `currency()`. `PaymentOrder.sum()` stays a decimal string (`"89.00"`); `currency()` and `formText()` may be `null`. `paylist()` maps a group id to its payment methods; when the ids are 0, 1, 2… the server sends a JSON array, whose items are keyed `"0"`, `"1"`, ….
`Paginator<T>`: `data()`, `currentPage()`, `lastPage()`, `perPage()`, `total()`, `from()`, `to()`, `nextPageUrl()`, ….

```java
Paginator<PaymentOrder> orders = client.user().paymentHistory().orders();
System.out.println(orders.total() + " orders, page " + orders.currentPage() + "/" + orders.lastPage());
```

## setWebhookUrl

Set the URL that receives SMS webhooks (see [Webhooks](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-java-api/webhooks)).

```java
void setWebhookUrl(String url)
```

```java
client.user().setWebhookUrl("https://example.com/onlinesim-hook");
```

Errors: `ApiException` `VALIDATION_ERROR` for an invalid URL; `getMessage()` holds the server's field messages.

## clearWebhookUrl

Remove the webhook URL, also from operations in progress.

```java
void clearWebhookUrl()
```

```java
client.user().clearWebhookUrl();
```

## webhookLogs

Webhook delivery log, newest first, 10 per page.

```java
Paginator<WebhookLog> webhookLogs()
Paginator<WebhookLog> webhookLogs(int page)
```

`WebhookLog`: `id()`, `userId()`, `webhookUrl()`, `type()`, `params()`, `status()`, `error()`, `createdAt()`, `updatedAt()` — `type()` is `receiving_sms` or `rent_sms`, `status()` is `success`, `fail` or `pending`, `params()` the payload that was sent (`WebhookPayload`).

```java
for (WebhookLog log : client.user().webhookLogs().data()) {
  System.out.println(log.createdAt() + " " + log.status() + " " + log.error());
}
```


# Webhooks

Set a URL with [`client.user().setWebhookUrl`](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-java-api/user#setwebhookurl). For each SMS the server POSTs a JSON body to it: `webhook_type` `receiving_sms` for numbers, `rent_sms` for rents. Delivery attempts are listed by [`client.user().webhookLogs`](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-java-api/user#webhooklogs).

## parseWebhook

Parse an inbound webhook body. A static method: no client needed.

```java
static WebhookPayload parseWebhook(String json)
```

Lenient: numeric fields may arrive as strings, missing or malformed fields become `null`, unknown fields are dropped. It throws `OnlineSimException` only when the input is not a JSON object.

```java
import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer;
import java.net.InetSocketAddress;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import ru.onlinesim.OnlineSim;
import ru.onlinesim.WebhookPayload;

public class WebhookServer {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    HttpServer server = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress(8080), 0);
    server.createContext("/onlinesim-hook", exchange -> {
      String body = new String(exchange.getRequestBody().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
      WebhookPayload hook = OnlineSim.parseWebhook(body);
      if ("receiving_sms".equals(hook.webhookType())) System.out.println(hook.operationId() + " " + hook.code());
      exchange.sendResponseHeaders(200, -1);
      exchange.close();
    });
    server.start();
  }
}
```

## Payload fields

| Accessor        | Type      | Description                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `webhookType()` | `String`  | `receiving_sms`, `rent_sms`, or `null` for anything else.                                                                    |
| `operationId()` | `Long`    | `tzid` of the operation or rent.                                                                                             |
| `userId()`      | `Long`    | Account id.                                                                                                                  |
| `countryCode()` | `Integer` | Country code of the number.                                                                                                  |
| `number()`      | `String`  | Numbers: `+` and the full number (`+79001234567`), or `hidden`. Rent: the full number in digits without `+` (`79001234567`). |
| `sender()`      | `String`  | Sender of the SMS, e.g. `VK`.                                                                                                |
| `message()`     | `String`  | Full SMS text.                                                                                                               |
| `code()`        | `String`  | Code extracted from the SMS.                                                                                                 |
| `timeStart()`   | `String`  | Numbers: when the operation was ordered. Rent: when the SMS arrived. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.                                  |
| `timeLeft()`    | `Long`    | Time left: seconds for numbers, minutes for rent.                                                                            |

Every accessor returns `null` when the field is missing or malformed.
